v.why: Adding a missing input-output residual shortcut helps far more than replacing an existing learned op on that edge.
In skip-dominated, parameter-free cells an extra identity path to the output degrades accuracy instead of helping.
Pooling-dominated cells lack convolutions, so an added identity shortcut further dilutes learned features and hurts.
Removing edge 0->3 when edge 2->3 is absent can disconnect or severely starve the output node.
Placing a conv on an empty input-output edge adds a new path rather than merely swapping ops.
Without the 0->3 shortcut, a skip on edge 2->3 supplies a needed residual path, whereas with it present the swap mainly removes conv capacity.
In skip-heavy cells edge 5 is often the only convolution, so replacing it with skip collapses learning capacity.
When edge 2->3 is absent, a conv on edge 1->3 becomes the main conv route into the output and adds much more value.
With edge 2->3 absent, turning the 1->3 conv into pooling removes the main conv path to the output.
Without edge 2->3, cutting edge 0->1 kills node 1 and leaves the output with only the input shortcut.

raw:
Selection rationale: most of the strongest interactions in the data involve connectivity, mainly whether the 0→3 skip path (edge 3) or the routes into node 3 (edges 4 and 5) already exist. Topology matters a lot here. The other strong pattern is that skip/pool-heavy cells, which have no convolutions, respond differently from conv-heavy cells.

1. **e3→skip_connect, higher when e3 is none.** This adds the input–output shortcut instead of replacing a learned op (experiments 11, 14, 17–20 vs 12, 13).
2. **e3→skip_connect, lower when e0 is skip_connect.** In parameter-free, skip-dominated cells, another identity path hurts a lot (experiment 15).
3. **e3→skip_connect, lower when e0 is avg_pool_3x3.** Pool-dominated cells behave the same way (experiment 16).
4. **e3→none, lower when e5 is none.** Removing edge 3 when edge 5 is absent can cut off or starve the output (experiments 22, 25 vs 21).
5. **e3→nor_conv_1x1, higher when e3 is none.** This creates a new path to the output instead of swapping one op for another (experiments 92, 95, 96, 98–100 vs 91, 93).
6. **e5→skip_connect, higher when e3 is none.** A 2→3 skip adds a needed residual path when the 0→3 shortcut is missing (experiments 72, 74 vs 71, 73).
7. **e5→skip_connect, lower when e0 is skip_connect.** Replacing the only conv in a skip-heavy cell removes most of its learning capacity (experiment 79).
8. **e4→nor_conv_3x3, higher when e5 is none.** With edge 5 absent, edge 4 becomes the main conv path into the output (experiments 58, 59).
9. **e4→avg_pool_3x3, lower when e5 is none.** Turning the main 1→3 conv path into pooling hurts most when no other conv feeds the output (experiments 85, 86).
10. **e0→none, lower when e5 is none.** Without edge 5, cutting edge 0 kills node 1, the remaining non-trivial route to the output (experiment 36).
